content:
Back in June, we noted that three Russian banks under U.S. sanctions had managed to get their client apps onto the App Store by circumventing review. Two months on, another example has climbed to the top of the iPhone App Store.

The latest case is K8CHEN PRO. The App Store listing presents it as an app for designing kitchens using augmented reality (AR).

But open the app and the facade quickly crumbles. The privacy policy linked from the App Store was generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator," which in itself should ring alarm bells.

In any case, this app is clearly T-Bank's client app. What I find interesting is that apps like this keep getting through Apple's review.

Once they attract enough attention and climb the App Store charts, anyone with eyes can see they shouldn't be there. It's a puzzling state of affairs.

Other examples from June can be found here and here.

Update: As expected, the app has been removed from the App Store.
